Fatty acids must be activated in the cytosol by binding to coenzyme A (forming acyl-CoA) before transport into mitochondria, but acyl-CoA cannot directly cross the inner mitochondrial membrane.  
Instead, the acyl group is transferred from CoA to carnitine, forming acylcarnitine, which is shuttled across the membrane by a translocase. Once inside, the acyl group is transferred back to CoA.  
Thus, the transport into mitochondria occurs bound to carnitine.
